🟢 Fortress balance sheet — net cash, >$1B liquidity, and a **$300M buyback executed then a +$500M buyback + dividend re-initiation** (Q4-25 → 2026-06-15). Net-cash special-situation: cash $674M vs total debt $68M (NET CASH ~$606M pre-sale).

- The persistent **"if" on Çöpler** from Q1-25 onward, paired with growing reclamation accruals, signaled management had internally written off the operate case long before the sale. The "discussions with the government" language was a managed wind-down, not a restart push.
- The **Q4-25 buyback + "share price does not reflect full value"** was the explicit pre-positioning for the divestiture: clear the overhang, return the cash, re-rate on the Americas multiple. The +$500M follow-on (2026-06-15) confirms a deliberate **shrink-the-share-count-into-the-cash-inflow** strategy.
- Capital-allocation discipline language is consistent (Rod's "we stay true to our criteria") and *backed by behavior* — they bought CC&V cheap, refused to overspend on Hod Maden, and chose a royalty over a build. This is an above-average allocator team.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**PIVOTING — and the pivot has already executed off-transcript.** SSRM has transformed from a Turkey-overhung mid-tier into a **clean Americas gold/silver producer (Marigold, CC&V, Seabee, Puna; ~450–535k GEO 2026 guide) + ~$1.5B incoming Çöpler cash + a 4% Hod Maden NSR royalty stub**, returning capital aggressively ($300M done, +$500M authorized, dividend reinstated).

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the four 2025 calls the story was remarkably consistent — and, in hindsight, misleading about where the company was actually heading.

**The story management told (all four quarters):** SSR was a turnaround with a stacked catalyst calendar. Every call, Executive Chairman Rod Antal recited the same priority list: (1) the "top priority" restart of Copler, the Turkish mine idled since a fatal February 2024 heap-leach-pad failure; (2) advancing Hod Maden, described repeatedly as "one of the most attractive, underdeveloped copper-gold projects in the sector," toward a construction decision; (3) integrating the newly acquired Cripple Creek & Victor (CC&V) mine in Colorado; and (4) organic growth at Marigold, Seabee, and Puna. # Forensic Dossier — SSR Mining (SSRM)

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the four 2025 calls the story was remarkably consistent — and, in hindsight, misleading about where the company was actually heading.

**The story management told (all four quarters):** SSR was a turnaround with a stacked catalyst calendar. Every call, Executive Chairman Rod Antal recited the same priority list: (1) the "top priority" restart of Copler, the Turkish mine idled since a fatal February 2024 heap-leach-pad failure; (2) advancing Hod Maden, described repeatedly as "one of the most attractive, underdeveloped copper-gold projects in the sector," toward a construction decision; (3) integrating the newly acquired Cripple Creek & Victor (CC&V) mine in Colorado; and (4) organic growth at Marigold, Seabee, and Puna. The refrain was "meaningful catalysts on the horizon over the next 12 months."

**What was emphasized at the start (first quarter 2025):** Copler restart optimism ("we remain confident of a restart"), the freshly closed CC&V deal, and heavy investment ($60–100M) in Hod Maden toward a build decision. The framing was offensive — spend now, grow later.

**What actually happened by the fourth-quarter call (February 2026):** The tone shifted from "restart is our top priority" to a much more guarded "we remain fully committed to a restart" with "really nothing to note since the last quarter" and site activity "wound down." Meanwhile two genuinely favorable things emerged that management leaned into: (a) a $300M share buyback authorization, justified explicitly because "our share price does not reflect the full value of our portfolio," and (b) two completed technical reports — CC&V (a 12-year mine life, $824M net present value) and Hod Maden (a $1.7B net present value, 39% internal rate of return).

# Forensic Dossier — SSR Mining (SSRM)

*A deep dive on management and the setup, built from four consecutive quarterly earnings calls (first quarter 2025 through the fourth-quarter-and-full-year 2025 call held February 18, 2026) cross-referenced against the screener's hard financials, and updated with the post-call corporate actions that reshaped the story after the last transcript.*

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the four 2025 calls the story was remarkably consistent — and, in hindsight, misleading about where the company was actually heading.

**The story management told (all four quarters):** SSR was a turnaround with a stacked catalyst calendar. Every call, Executive Chairman Rod Antal recited the same priority list: (1) the "top priority" restart of Copler, the Turkish mine idled since a fatal February 2024 heap-leach-pad failure; (2) advancing Hod Maden, described repeatedly as "one of the most attractive, underdeveloped copper-gold projects in the sector," toward a construction decision; (3) integrating the newly acquired Cripple Creek & Victor (CC&V) mine in Colorado; and (4) organic growth at Marigold, Seabee, and Puna. **What was emphasized at the start (first quarter 2025):** Copler restart optimism ("we remain confident of a restart"), the freshly closed CC&V deal, and heavy investment ($60–100M) in Hod Maden toward a build decision. The framing was offensive — spend now, grow later.

**What actually happened by the fourth-quarter call (February 2026):** The tone shifted from "restart is our top priority" to a much more guarded "we remain fully committed to a restart" with "really nothing to note since the last quarter" and site activity "wound down." # Forensic Dossier — SSR Mining (SSRM)

*A deep dive on management and the setup, built from four consecutive quarterly earnings calls (first quarter 2025 through the fourth-quarter-and-full-year 2025 call held February 18, 2026) cross-referenced against the screener's hard financials, and updated with the post-call corporate actions that reshaped the story after the last transcript.*

**One-sentence read:** A mid-tier gold-and-silver miner that spent 2025 telling a "rebuild and grow" story around three big projects — a restart of its idled Turkish Copler mine, a build decision at the Hod Maden copper-gold project, and organic mine-life extensions — and then, in the four months *after* the last call, quietly reversed two-thirds of that story by agreeing to sell both Turkish assets for cash and a royalty, pivoting from a builder to a cash-rich, capital-returning Americas producer.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the four 2025 calls the story was remarkably consistent — and, in hindsight, misleading about where the company was actually heading.

**The story management told (all four quarters):** SSR was a turnaround with a stacked catalyst calendar. Every call, Executive Chairman Rod Antal recited the same priority list: (1) the "top priority" restart of Copler, the Turkish mine idled since a fatal February 2024 heap-leach-pad failure; (2) advancing Hod Maden, described repeatedly as "one of the most attractive, underdeveloped copper-gold projects in the sector," toward a construction decision; (3) integrating the newly acquired Cripple Creek & Victor (CC&V) mine in Colorado; and (4) organic growth at Marigold, Seabee, and Puna. The refrain was "meaningful catalysts on the horizon over the next 12 months."

**What was emphasized at the start (first quarter 2025):** Copler restart optimism ("we remain confident of a restart"), the freshly closed CC&V deal, and heavy investment ($60–100M) in Hod Maden toward a build decision. The framing was offensive — spend now, grow later.

**What actually happened by the fourth-quarter call (February 2026):** The tone shifted from "restart is our top priority" to a much more guarded "we remain fully committed to a restart" with "really nothing to note since the last quarter" and site activity "wound down." Meanwhile two genuinely favorable things emerged that management leaned into: (a) a $300M share buyback authorization, justified explicitly because "our share price does not reflect the full value of our portfolio," and (b) two completed technical reports — CC&V (a 12-year mine life, $824M net present value) and Hod Maden (a $1.7B net present value, 39% internal rate of return).

**The pivot the transcripts do NOT contain (post-call, verified live):** Within weeks of the February call, SSR agreed to *sell* Copler outright — an 80% stake to Cengiz Holding for $1.5B in cash (binding memorandum March 4, 2026; definitive agreement March 24, 2026; expected to close before the end of the third quarter of 2026). In May 2026 it also agreed to *sell* its Hod Maden stake and operatorship to Lidya Mines for a 4.0% net smelter royalty rather than build the mine itself. So two of the three pillars of the 2025 "builder" narrative were monetized, not executed. This is the single most important fact about SSR today and it post-dates every transcript in the file.

**Net:** the narrative arc is a builder-to-harvester pivot. The 2025 calls sold a growth-and-restart story; the 2026 corporate actions cashed it in.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (quarter) | The hard numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong free cash flow generation" all year | Full-year 2025 free cash flow $252M reported; trailing-twelve-month free cash flow $482M (screener, as of March 31, 2026); price-to-free-cash-flow ~27x | **Matches, but the multiple is rich.** Cash generation is real and improving, driven by a $3,500–4,142/oz gold tape, not volume. |

| "Long-lived, significant" assets; "one of the most attractive" projects | Return on equity 3.2%, return on invested capital 2.2% | **Diverges sharply.** For a gold miner earning through a record-price tape, low-single-digit returns on capital are weak — the drag is the idle Copler asset, remediation costs, and heavy growth capital that earned nothing. |

**Trajectory: Declining on Copler, Rising on capital returns — a split.**

- **The Copler restart guidance had no credibility because there was never a date.** For four straight quarters management refused to commit to any timeline — defensible given a foreign regulator, but it means the single biggest 2025 "catalyst" was never a scheduled event. **Sandbagging pattern:** mild and on the operating assets (CC&V under-promised, over-delivered). No sandbagging on Copler — that was genuine open-ended uncertainty, later cut short by the decision to sell.

The same two analysts — Scotiabank's Ovais Habib and National Bank's Don DeMarco, plus CIBC's Cosmos Chiu — pushed on the same three things every quarter:

1. **"When does Copler restart?"** — asked in some form on every call; never answered with a date. Management insisted they were "mutually exclusive." In the end SSR sold *both*, so the linkage question was more prescient than management's answer implied.
3. **"How much upside is really in CC&V?"** — analysts pushed for optimization detail; management kept deferring to a forthcoming technical report ("just a placeholder at the moment"). What analysts under-weighted: the balance sheet and the possibility of a *sale* of the Turkish assets. The Q&A was fixated on restart mechanics; nobody modeled the $1.5B cash exit that actually happened.

---

🔴 **Return on invested capital of 2.2% and return on equity of 3.2%** during the best gold-price environment in history — capital was tied up in non-earning assets (idle Copler, Hod Maden development, remediation).

🟢 **CC&V acquisition already paid back** — $100M in, ~$115M of asset-level free cash flow out within a year; a genuinely good capital-allocation decision.

The May 2026 sale to Lidya for a royalty confirmed it: SSR wanted the upside without the build risk or the Turkish exposure.

**Classification: PIVOTING (builder to harvester).**

SSR has, in the four months since its last earnings call, transformed from a mid-tier miner carrying a heavy Turkish-restart-and-build burden into a debt-free, cash-rich, pure-Americas gold-and-silver producer returning capital aggressively. The Copler sale ($1.5B cash, definitive agreement, expected to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026) and the Hod Maden royalty sale remove the two largest sources of risk and non-earning capital, and the proceeds fund buybacks and a restored dividend.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the four 2025 calls the story was remarkably consistent — and, in hindsight, misleading about where the company was actually heading.

**The story management told (all four quarters):** SSR was a turnaround with a stacked catalyst calendar. Every call, Executive Chairman Rod Antal recited the same priority list: (1) the "top priority" restart of Copler, the Turkish mine idled since a fatal February 2024 heap-leach-pad failure; (2) advancing Hod Maden, described repeatedly as "one of the most attractive, underdeveloped copper-gold projects in the sector," toward a construction decision; (3) integrating the newly acquired Cripple Creek & Victor (CC&V) mine in Colorado; and (4) organic growth at Marigold, Seabee, and Puna. **What was emphasized at the start (first quarter 2025):** Copler restart optimism ("we remain confident of a restart"), the freshly closed CC&V deal, and heavy investment ($60–100M) in Hod Maden toward a build decision. The framing was offensive — spend now, grow later.

**What actually happened by the fourth-quarter call (February 2026):** The tone shifted from "restart is our top priority" to a much more guarded "we remain fully committed to a restart" with "really nothing to note since the last quarter" and site activity "wound down." Across the four 2025 calls the story was remarkably consistent — and, in hindsight, misleading about where the company was actually heading.

**The story management told (all four quarters):** SSR was a turnaround with a stacked catalyst calendar. Every call, Executive Chairman Rod Antal recited the same priority list: (1) the "top priority" restart of Copler, the Turkish mine idled since a fatal February 2024 heap-leach-pad failure; (2) advancing Hod Maden, described repeatedly as "one of the most attractive, underdeveloped copper-gold projects in the sector," toward a construction decision; (3) integrating the newly acquired Cripple Creek & Victor (CC&V) mine in Colorado; and (4) organic growth at Marigold, Seabee, and Puna.
